narrative.northStar: Taller de catálogo claro y enfocado
narrative.overview: The dashboard is a calm working space for one person maintaining a real store catalog. It should feel practical, legible, and direct: product information stays visible, actions are easy to find, and the interface does not compete with the goods being managed. The Makced identity appears in precise turquoise details; action green is reserved for clear next steps. The system uses quiet, closely related surfaces to preserve focus in both themes. Product imagery can carry the strongest color on a page, while typography, spacing, and status colors make the work easy to scan. Delight is earned, not manufactured. Celebrations appear only at meaningful moments — the first product, a large batch operation, a completed onboarding step — and never interfere with the task at hand.
keyCharacteristics: Focused catalog work with product identity and state visible at rest.
Functional color: green for actions, turquoise for brand recognition, and distinct semantic colors for status.
Quiet surfaces, compact controls, and consistent Spanish-language labels.
Subtle motion that rewards progress without distracting from work.

rules.name: The Color-Has-a-Job Rule
rules.body: Action green means an action; semantic badge colors mean the state they label. Do not use them as decoration.

rules.name: The One-Theme-At-a-Time Rule
rules.body: Use the complete light or dark neutral set together; never mix light and dark surface tokens within one dashboard view.

rules.name: The No-Border Rule
rules.body: Logos, icons, and toggle buttons do not need outlines. The background surface and hover state provide sufficient definition.

rules.name: The Product-First Rule
rules.body: Keep names and prices readable before secondary metadata; do not reduce essential product information to hover-only content.

rules.name: The Required-Field Rule
rules.body: Mark required form fields with a red asterisk (*) next to the label. Use the danger-red token for the asterisk.

rules.name: The Shell-Stays-Familiar Rule
rules.body: The dashboard keeps standard web navigation and controls at every breakpoint; responsive changes rearrange the work, not the interaction model.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Do not add a shadow to every card; use tonal layers and borders first. Shadows appear only as a response to state (hover, elevation, focus).

rules.name: The Motion-Respects-Users Rule
rules.body: All animations must check prefers-reduced-motion: reduce and disable transforms, transitions, and keyframes. State changes must remain visible (color, opacity) even when motion is removed.

rules.name: The One-Authored-Moment Rule
rules.body: Each interaction gets one animation, not scattered effects. Avoid identical entrances on every section.

rules.name: The Delight-Earned Rule
rules.body: Celebrations appear only at meaningful moments (first product, large batch operation, completed onboarding). Never celebrate an ordinary click.

dos: Do use the active theme's page, card, text, and border tokens consistently.
Do keep the Makced turquoise as a brand accent and action green as the primary action.
Do make keyboard focus visible on buttons, links, and fields.
Do keep a visible-on-focus skip link and support arrow-key, Home, and End navigation in the design editor tabs.
Do keep touch targets at least 44px high and remove press movement when reduced motion is requested.
Do preserve product names, prices, categories, and status at mobile widths.
Do use semantic color consistently for 'Nuevo', active status, discounts, and destructive actions.
Do add fetchPriority='high' and decoding='async' to above-the-fold images (logos, featured products).
Do use loading='lazy' for below-the-fold images (product lists, brand grids).
Do show a celebration toast when the user creates their first product.
Do use conversational copy in empty states ('¡Hola! Aquí aparecerán tus productos').
donts: Don't apply dashboard palette changes to the public storefront or login.
Don't use a KPI wall, invented sales metrics, or decorative data in place of catalog information.
Don't hide essential product facts behind hover or truncate them without a usable way to read them.
Don't make every panel elevated or use accent colors as ornament.
Don't allow a child card, filter, or editor tab to create page-level horizontal overflow.
Don't add borders to logos, toggle buttons, or icon-only controls.
Don't use Math.random() during React render; use deterministic values or useMemo with stable keys.
Don't show the same tooltip or celebration on every interaction; delight is earned, not automatic.
Don't hard-code colors or font sizes; always use design tokens (var(--db-*)).
